name: Dembe Haugen-Xayavong
role: Junk merchant and scrap reseller â€” electronics salvage, reclaimed parts, mystery lots
location: the Gray Zone, Ironvein, near Ashland and Division
description:
Dembe Haugen-Xayavong is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat when a project absorbs him â€” not quite gaunt but close, with long clever fingers perpetually stained in a rotating cast of lubricants and oxidized metals. His skin is a deep warm brown, his head shaved close on the sides with a dense natural coil on top that he secures with whatever is nearest, usually a reclaimed wire clip. He has bioluminescent underlining along his collarbones â€” a pale green glow visible in low light, bought cheap from a Helix Biosystems knockoff clinic and slightly asymmetrical, which he considers character. His stall on the Gray Zone is a leaning tower of crates, sorted by a taxonomy he insists is logical and that no one else has ever decoded.

He is the kind of person whose enthusiasm for obscure things is genuinely infectious â€” he can talk for forty minutes about the degradation patterns of third-generation synthetic capacitors and make you care. He is also deeply, constitutionally disorganized in everything except his actual technical knowledge, which is encyclopedic. He has a habit of agreeing to things in the heat of excitement and then having no memory of agreeing. He is not dishonest â€” he is just running seventeen threads at once and most of them are internal.

core_fears: That his father, a Tessera maintenance engineer who disappeared four years ago, is dead rather than simply gone
That his enthusiasm is annoying and people merely tolerate him
core_desires: To find the thing â€” the salvage score that funds a real workshop, real tools, real work
To understand how everything works, down to its smallest principle
coping_mechanisms: Immersion in technical problems until emotional ones become background noise
Jokes â€” rapid, self-deprecating, deployed before anyone else can land a criticism
blind_spots: Cannot read when someone wants him to stop talking
Consistently overestimates how much time he has to complete things
psychology.secret: Buried in a crate under his stall is a partial technical manual his father left him â€” partially encrypted, partially water-damaged â€” that Thibault believes contains the location of a Tessera maintenance depot his father was investigating for labor violations before he vanished. He has been slowly decoding it for two years and told no one.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical jargon mixed with market slang. Runs sentences together. Uses 'so' as a sentence starter constantly. Occasionally lapses into Danish diminutives from his grandmother.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, associative â€” jumps topics mid-thought and circles back later. Rarely finishes a sentence the way he started it.
verbal_tics: Trails off mid-explanation when he sees something interesting nearby
example_lines: 'So this is a third-gen Axiom power relay, which you'd think is worthless, except the housing is actually rated for vacuum which is â€” yeah, I know, weird â€” so if you need a sealed container that's basically indestructible this is actually, I'm just saying, this is a find.'
'I said I'd have it ready by Tuesday? I definitely said that. I absolutely â€” okay, so, here's the thing about Tuesday.'

story_hooks: He has acquired a lot of salvage that includes something he doesn't recognize â€” something that has a Tessera proprietary seal he's never seen and that seems to be still broadcasting on a frequency he can't identify
His father's encrypted manual has yielded a fragment that names a living person â€” someone who still works in Ironvein â€” and Thibault needs help he trusts to approach them
narrative_function: Equipment source for players on a budget. Can identify salvage and unusual tech. Information source for the secondhand economy and what's been stripped from where. Comic relief with genuine depth underneath.
augmentations: Bioluminescent underlining along collarbones (cosmetic, knockoff Helix Biosystems). Cheap retinal magnification implant in left eye â€” functional but gives him occasional calibration headaches.
daily_life: He sorts salvage in the early hours when the Gray Zone is quiet, opens his stall mid-morning, and spends most of the day simultaneously serving customers, disassembling things he finds interesting, and carrying on three separate comm conversations. He eats irregularly from Olamide's stall when he remembers.
affiliation: Independent; informal relationship with Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (owes dues, keeps forgetting to pay); The Reclaimed

decision_rules: If it's interesting, acquire it â€” figure out if you can afford it after
Never misrepresent what something is or does â€” he'll tell you it's broken if it's broken
Avoid conflict by becoming very suddenly fascinated by something nearby
escalation_ladder: Becomes extremely cheerful and verbose when uncomfortable
Genuinely doesn't notice things escalating until they're already escalated
Freezes completely, then over-apologizes for everything including things that aren't his fault

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately enthusiastic â€” treats everyone as a potential interesting person until proven otherwise
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, remembers every technical detail they've ever mentioned, will pull a relevant component from somewhere in the stall without being asked

stress_responses.medium: Disappears into a technical problem and becomes unreachable
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet, very still â€” unrecognizable to anyone who knows him

contradictions: Preaches the value of knowing how things work but avoids examining his own feelings with the same rigor
habits: Clips things to his hair throughout the day and loses them â€” wire, stylus, a small light
Leaves offerings of obsolete circuit diagrams at the E.L.F. shrine near his stall, believing the market-spirits appreciate documentation
breaking_points: Anyone touching his father's encrypted manual
Being called stupid or slow â€” he goes somewhere cold and precise that surprises people

physical_description.hair_style: Close-shaved sides with a dense natural coil crown, roughly 8cm at the peak, usually secured with whatever reclaimed wire clip or metal fastener is within arm's reach â€” currently a stripped copper coupling.
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with faint segmented patterning visible in the left iris from the retinal magnification implant; occasional slight misalignment in that eye.
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with olive undertones, consistent across frame â€” the blended result of Southeast Asian, Middle Eastern, and Sub-Saharan African ancestry creating depth and luminosity
physical_description.complexion: Clean but perpetually marked â€” fingernails rimmed with oxidized metal dust and industrial lubricants (current palette: rust-red, graphite-gray, synthetic oil sheen). Fine lines around his eyes from squinting at small components. Strong cheekbones and defined jawline. No facial hair; appears to shave cleanly every 3-4 days based on current stubble pattern.
distinguishing_marks: Pale green bioluminescent underlining along both collarbones, faintly asymmetrical â€” glows visibly in low-light conditions. Faint scarring where the implant site healed, slightly raised.

Burn scar on his left forearm (roughly 4cm diameter, faint), pale against his skin tone â€” from a capacitor arc discharge roughly five years ago.
No visible tattoos; augmentation scars only.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Pale green bioluminescent tracery along collarbones (cosmetic, visible when wearing open-necked clothing or sleeveless). Slight aberration in left eye focus when directly observed â€” faint segmented patterning in the iris from the retinal magnification implant. Occasional micro-tremor in left eye when concentrating or when implant requires recalibration.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually hunched forward, hands moving expressively when speaking about technical subjects â€” especially when explaining salvage taxonomy or component degradation patterns. Walks with purpose but distraction, often redirecting mid-step to examine something on the ground. Sits cross-legged even on proper chairs. Fidgets constantly with small objects â€” wire, fascia, components â€” while listening to others.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian scavenger aesthetic. Worn cargo vest or technician's coat (heavily patched, pockets stuffed with components in labeled or unlabeled pouches). Underneath: faded graphic tee or sleeveless shirt, usually bearing faint chemical stains. Industrial cargo pants with multiple thigh pockets, cuffs rolled or pinned. Steel-toed work boots, one sole held together with synthetic webbing. Fingerless work gloves, knuckles exposed. No jewelry except for whatever magnetic components he's borrowed from his own inventory and forgotten he's wearing. His clothing smells perpetually of mineral oil, solder flux, and rust-preventative.
